dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin.
Hi, um, yes, hello. My name's David Okafor. I'm calling about a tree that's down, a big one, across the road. Well, I guess I'm not totally sure who I'm supposed to call for that.
Okay, you called the right place to start. Where's the tree at?

It's on Gidley Street, in front of one ninety. That's the Fifth Ward, kind of down toward the, um, the end where it bends. I'm on speakerphone, by the way, I'm in my car, so tell me if I'm breaking up.
No, you're coming through fine. One ninety Gidley. And you said it's across the road. Is it all the way across?

Yeah, it's all the way across. It's blocking both lanes. Nothing's getting through, not even a small car. Well, maybe a bike, but that's it. It's a big trunk, the thing's got to be two feet thick or more, and then all the branches are spread out over the pavement.
Got it. Is it on any wires, or are there wires down near it?

Um, no, I don't think so. I looked and I don't see any wires on the ground. There's a line up above, along the pole, but it looks like it's still up there and not touching the tree. I stayed back, though, I didn't get too close.
Good, stay back from it. Okay, writing this down. Large tree, both lanes blocked, one ninety Gidley, no wires on the ground that you can see. When did this come down?

So it was the storm. The coastal storm from Friday into Saturday, two days ago. I think it came down sometime Saturday, because Friday night it was still standing. I noticed it Saturday morning and figured somebody would come, and then, well, it's Monday and it's still there.
Yeah, we've got a lot of calls stacked up since the weekend. Crews are working through the main routes first and then the side streets.

Right, okay. That makes sense. So the other thing I wanted to ask is, um, who actually handles it? Is it the city, or is it the property owner, or is it the electric company? Because I wasn't sure whose tree it is.

Good question. So if the tree's on city property or it's in the street right-of-way, like a street tree, then that's us, the city. If it came off a private yard, the removal of the tree itself is usually on the owner. But when it's blocking a public road, we'll come out and clear enough to open the road regardless, and then the owner deals with the rest. If it's on a wire, that's the utility.
Okay. Okay, so I don't have to figure out whose it is before I call.
Nope, you don't. That's what the report's for. We'll send somebody to look at it and sort that out. Do you happen to know which yard it came out of?

Um, well, I think it's from the lot across the street from me, the one with the gray fence, but I honestly can't say for sure. It's kind of lying right in the middle of the road, so it could be from either side. I own my house, it's not mine, I know that much. I've only got a little maple out front and that's fine.
Alright. I'll put down possibly from the lot across from one ninety, ownership unknown. That's plenty for the crew.

Great. And, um, just so you know, the reason I'm pushing a little on this, my workplace is hosting an inspection later this week. Thursday, I think. And a bunch of people are coming in from out of town, and I'm one of the people helping get things ready. So I need the street to be passable, because I'm not sure how else I'd get through.

Okay, I'll note that there's a time concern. I can't promise you it'll be cleared today, but I'll flag it as a blocked road, which puts it higher up the list than a tree that's just down in somebody's yard.
That would be great, thank you. Do you think it would be, like, today or tomorrow? Or is it more of a, um, a few days?
Blocked roads usually get hit within a day or two, so I'd say you're looking at today or tomorrow, with Wednesday being the outside edge. Hopefully well before Thursday.
Okay. That's good. That's workable.
Now, do you want a call back when the crew has been out, or are you good to just watch for it?
Um, a call back would be good, actually. If someone could let me know when it's cleared, or if it turns out it's not the city's.
Sure. What's the best number?
It's four oh one, five five five, zero one nine two.
Four oh one, five five five, zero one nine two. And that's under David Okafor, O-K-A-F-O-R?
Yep, that's right. O-K-A-F-O-R.

Perfect. So I've got the tree down across both lanes at one ninety Gidley Street, from the storm Friday into Saturday, no wires on the ground, possibly from the lot across the street, and you'd like a callback at that number. Anything else on it?
Um, well, one more thing. If I see somebody else down the road with a tree down, is it the same number? Like, if I want to tell a neighbor where to report it.

Yep, same line. They can call Public Works here during the day, and if it's a tree on a wire or anything that's dangerous, like sparking, they should call the utility and the emergency line right away. But a regular downed tree, this is the place.
Okay, that's good to know. I'll pass that along.
Sounds good. We'll get somebody out there as soon as we can, David.
Thanks a lot, Kevin. I appreciate it.
No problem. Take care, and drive safe.
Will do. Bye.
